page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is capped at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile that leans toward the lower tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests falls into the bottom 25%, with scores of 1105.78 and 5878.39 respectively. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are positioned in the bottom 10% and 25% brackets. However, memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks achieves average tier performance, registering 39.24 GB/sec for read operations and 34.3 GB/sec for write operations. Large-scale LLM inference is highly constrained, with the medium 7B model achieving only 5.04 tokens/sec for text generation, though small 135M model inference remains average at 99.23 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on dedicated Intel Xeon hardware, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency compute power. The lack of local storage and low baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps are notable tradeoffs. This instance is best suited for workloads such as caching layers, small-to-medium database deployments with moderate transaction volumes, and memory-bound data processing tasks that do not demand high CPU throughput.
